rationale: § 20 satisfies the preferred position in full: Vendor expressly defends, indemnifies and holds harmless Customer and its Affiliates against third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables (20.1), and against claims arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard procedure is present — prompt notice, reasonable cooperation (at the indemnifying Party's expense) and control of the defence, with a settlement-consent protection (20.4). Customer's reciprocal indemnity is properly narrow, covering only unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized and Customer's violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions (20.3). Beyond the preferred level, 20.5 adds procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and § 21.3 treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims outside the liability cap, which is better for us than the fallback 3× super-cap. No redline required.

quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
rationale: The IP package meets the preferred position in full. § 14.2 gives Customer ownership of each Deliverable and a present assignment by Vendor of all worldwide right, title and interest. § 14.3 confirms Vendor retains only Vendor Technology (defined in § 1.9 as its pre-existing technology, excluding Customer Data and Customer's pre-existing IP), and applies the § 13.2 licence to embedded Vendor Technology, which is "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" and permits use, modification, derivative works and contractor support for Customer's business. § 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data and Customer-provided material, with "No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer" — processing to deliver, secure, support and improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation, so the Vendor-side data licence is appropriately confined; § 15.1 further bars sale, advertising use, data combination and model training. § 14.4 provides that no jointly owned IP is created absent a separate signed instrument that fixes exploitation rights, so there is no unrestricted joint ownership. Minor points noted but not redlined: Deliverable ownership is expressed as "subject to payment of the applicable Fees", and § 15.1's "as permitted by this Agreement" is a general cross-reference rather than a standalone licence. No assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor exists, so no change is required.

quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form.
rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position. Transition obligations are triggered "[u]pon expiry or termination for any reason" with no carve-out for Vendor termination for cause (11.1); Vendor must provide up to six months of transition assistance (11.1); Customer Data must be returned within thirty days in a "complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format" (11.2), and Vendor must securely delete remaining Customer Data and certify deletion in writing only after Customer confirms successful return (11.3). Two immaterial variances, both favourable to us, are noted rather than flagged: assistance is priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form rather than Vendor's then-current rates, and the thirty-day return clock runs from Customer's request rather than the termination date, leaving timing under our control. Sections 10 and 15 contain no conflicting deletion or data-retention mechanic, and 16.3 expressly leaves Customer Data governed by Sections 11 and 15. No redline required.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it.
rationale: Section 19 meets, and in most respects exceeds, the playbook fallback and substantially satisfies the preferred position. 19.1 warrants that Services (defined in 1.8 to include the hosted software) will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner and that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and specifications, with no time limit on that undertaking; 19.2 gives Deliverables ninety days after delivery or acceptance (above the 90-day software / 30-day services fallback floors) and warrants Hosted Services conformance throughout the subscription term, which under 8.2 runs for the Order Form initial term and successive twelve-month renewals. 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law and a no-malicious-code warranty, and 19.4 supplies real remedies: prompt re-performance, repair or replacement, and a refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The 19.5 disclaimer is mutual and expressly does not limit any express warranty, so it does not swallow the warranty. Two minor points fall short of preferred wording only and are not redlined: the deliverable conformance period is ninety days rather than twelve months (the hosted software is covered for the full term), and the malicious-code warranty is qualified by "intentionally introduced by Vendor".

quote: 18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.
rationale: Section 18 meets the preferred position in full: CGL of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, professional E&O of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability of USD 5,000,000 (granted unconditionally, so it covers Vendor's processing of Customer Data), with certificates of insurance provided on request under 18.2. The clause is favourable to us in additional respects (employer's liability, primary coverage, notice of cancellation, and confirmation that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities), so no redline is warranted.
